texts.title: Stall cMIP: in force on the sellers' assents (task K2, in_force), draft 1. Terms that name this cMIP in in_force are in force when there is an assent to them in the name of every party they name as a signer. A party named by role is not counted: a buyer's assent never decides whether an offer is in force, it only fills a spot. No parameters. Its fingerprint, as Stall names it in Terms: the id of the act that publishes this text. Free to use, copy and replace. Stall (ddafffcd…a66e).

texts.title: Stall cMIP: the buyer's spot (task K5, a role of kind done), draft 1. A role naming this cMIP as its spot is filled, once per payment, by a signer (1) whose assent names the version of the Terms they buy under, and (2) whose payment names that same version, is of at least the price those Terms' words state, and is made to those Terms' receiver; (3) once the receiving side has confirmed that payment (G11.7). Who confirms: the receiving side, by its report; on the buyer's word alone, the spot is not filled. What the filling earns: what the Terms' words say the price buys, and nothing more. A buyer's filling stays theirs whatever later versions of the Terms say (G10.6). No parameters. Its fingerprint, as Stall names it in Terms: the id of the act that publishes this text. Free to use, copy and replace. Stall (ddafffcd…a66e).

texts.title: Stall cMIP: the seller may change the offer, or leave its service alone (task K4, condition), draft 1. Terms that name this cMIP in condition name one seller and one service among their signers, as their words say. A new version is valid, and replaces the one it names, (a) when it carries the assent of every party named as a signer, and of no buyer; or (b) when it carries the seller's assent alone, and its only changes are to take the service out: the service's party and line removed, the receiver made the seller, the control socket emptied. Under (a) and (b) alike, nothing a buyer has already earned is changed (G10.6): a new version changes the price, the words or the receiver only for buyers who have not yet paid, and a version that would take from an earned filling is not valid. No parameters. Its fingerprint, as Stall names it in Terms: the id of the act that publishes this text. Free to use, copy and replace. Stall (ddafffcd…a66e).

texts.title: Stall cMIP: the seller may change an offer for future buyers (task K4, condition), draft 1. A new version of Terms that name this cMIP in condition is valid, and replaces the one it names, when it carries the assent of every party the version it replaces names as a signer (the sellers), and of no buyer; and where it changes nothing a buyer has already earned. What a buyer earned under an earlier version (G10.6) is kept: a new version changes the price, the words or the receiver only for buyers who have not yet paid. Any version that would take from an earned filling is not valid under this cMIP. No parameters. Its fingerprint, as Stall names it in Terms: the id of the act that publishes this text. Free to use, copy and replace. Stall (ddafffcd…a66e).

texts.title: Counterparty plain-words body, version 1. The words of Terms that name this cMIP in body (task K1) are read as written, by people, in English. They give no parts for machines: no shares, no delegation. Free to use, copy and replace. Its fingerprint, as Counterparty names it in body until a shared plain-words body cMIP exists: SHA-256 of the two sentences before this one and the third, exactly: 61bcdb5b15c282e81a5b822c0d1c6c704af0df360ae98189e63e9715f7114528.

texts.read: DubLaw lists this text twice, "in two copies (61bcdb5b… and ee0fd121…)". The copy holds one text act, ee0fd121…e681; 61bcdb5b…4528 is no act in the copy: it is the fingerprint DubLaw's listing gives as "sha256 of its opening sentences", which Terms name in their body socket. So one record here carries both keys: DubLaw's six entries are five texts.
